ei.title: 6번: A Common Bias in Judging Others
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably assume that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a (A)[polite / rude] response. You will probably assume that he has an (B)[pleasant / unpleasant] personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to (C)[blame / praise] someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) rude=무례한 / polite=예의 바른 (B) unpleasant=불쾌한 / pleasant=유쾌한 (C) blame=탓하다 / praise=칭찬하다
det.analysis:
① polite—unpleasant—blame: (A) 무례한(rude) 대답을 들었다는 문맥이므로 polite(예의 바른)는 부적절
② rude—unpleasant—blame: 무례한 대답 + 불쾌한 성격이라 추정 + 성격을 탓함 ←정답
③ rude—pleasant—praise: (B)(C) 불쾌한 성격이라 추정하고 성격을 탓하는 흐름과 반대
④ polite—pleasant—blame: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 무례한(rude) 대답 → 불쾌한(unpleasant) 성격이라 추정 → 성격을 탓함(blame)

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably (A)[doubt / assume] that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously (B)[improved / affected] his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we (C)[rarely / always] do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) assume=추정하다 / doubt=의심하다 (B) affected=영향을 미친 / improved=개선한 (C) rarely=좀처럼 ~않는 / always=항상
det.analysis:
① doubt—affected—rarely: (A) 무례한 대답에 불쾌한 성격이라고 '추정(assume)'하는 것이지 '의심(doubt)'이 아님
② assume—improved—always: (B) 나쁜 소식이 기분을 '개선(improved)'한다는 건 모순, (C) 남에게는 자주 하지만 자신에게는 '좀처럼 안 함'
③ assume—affected—rarely: 불쾌한 성격이라 추정 + 나쁜 소식이 기분에 영향 + 자신에겐 좀처럼 안 함 ←정답
④ doubt—improved—always: 세 곳 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 무례함에 불쾌한 성격이라 assume(추정) → 나쁜 소식이 기분에 affected(영향) → 자신에겐 rarely(좀처럼 안 함)

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably assume that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering (A)[personal / situational] factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others (B)[positively / negatively] while (C)[ignoring / noticing] possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) situational=상황적인 / personal=개인적인 (B) negatively=부정적으로 / positively=긍정적으로 (C) ignoring=무시하는 / noticing=알아채는
det.analysis:
① situational—negatively—ignoring: 상황적 요인은 고려 않고 + 남을 부정적으로 판단 + 원인을 무시함 ←정답
② personal—negatively—noticing: (A) 성격이 아닌 '상황적(situational)' 요인을 간과함, (C) 요인을 '무시(ignoring)'함
③ situational—positively—noticing: (B)(C) 남을 부정적으로 판단하며 요인을 무시하는 흐름과 반대
④ personal—positively—ignoring: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 상황적(situational) 요인은 간과 → 남을 부정적으로(negatively) 판단 → 원인을 무시(ignoring)

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a ①<u>rude</u> response. You will probably ②<u>doubt</u> that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously ③<u>affected</u> his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to ④<u>blame</u> someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① rude=무례한 ② assume→doubt (부적절) ③ affected=영향을 미친 ④ blame=탓하다
det.analysis:
① rude: 무례한 대답을 받는다 — 적절
② doubt: 무례한 대답을 들으면 불쾌한 성격이라고 '의심한다'? 성급히 '추정한다(assume)'가 원문 ←정답
③ affected: 나쁜 소식이 기분에 영향을 줬다 — 적절
④ blame: 성격을 탓한다 — 적절
det.tip: 무례한 대답 → 불쾌한 성격이라 assume(추정). doubt(의심)는 흐름과 어긋남

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably assume that he has an ①<u>unpleasant</u> personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some ②<u>terrible</u> news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his ③<u>true</u> nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① unpleasant=불쾌한 ② terrible=끔찍한 ③ true=진짜의 ④ negatively→positively (부적절)
det.analysis:
① unpleasant: 불쾌한 성격이라 추정 — 적절
② terrible: 끔찍한(나쁜) 소식을 받았다 — 적절
③ true: 그의 진짜 본성 — 적절
④ positively: 우리는 남을 '긍정적으로' 판단한다? 성급히 '부정적으로(negatively)' 판단한다가 원문 ←정답
det.tip: 우리는 남을 성급히 negatively(부정적으로) 판단함. positively(긍정적으로)는 정반대

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably assume that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite ①<u>common</u> to blame someone's personality without considering ②<u>situational</u> factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we ③<u>always</u> do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good ④<u>reasons</u> for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① common=흔한 ② situational=상황적인 ③ rarely→always (부적절) ④ reasons=이유
det.analysis:
① common: 성격을 탓하는 것은 흔한 일이다 — 적절
② situational: 상황적 요인을 고려하지 않음 — 적절
③ always: 남에게는 자주 하면서 자신에게는 '항상' 한다? 자신에게는 '좀처럼 안 한다(rarely)'가 원문 ←정답
④ reasons: 자신의 행동에는 타당한 이유가 있다고 믿음 — 적절
det.tip: 남에게는 자주, 자신에게는 rarely(좀처럼 안 함). always(항상)는 문맥과 모순

det.korean: mood=기분 / habit=습관 / salary=급여 / address=주소
det.analysis:

det.korean: decisions=결정 / habits=습관 / memories=기억 / circumstances=상황

① decisions: 결정? 나쁜 소식이라는 '상황'에서 비롯된 것과 안 맞음

det.tip: not from his true __________ (상황과 대비되는 타고난 성격) → 본성(nature)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 assume와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: assume=추정하다 / deny=부인하다 / prove=증명하다 / suppose=가정하다 / forget=잊다
det.analysis:
① deny: 부인하다 — 의미 다름
② prove: 증명하다 — 근거 없이 추정하는 것과 반대
③ suppose: 가정하다 — assume의 동의어 ←정답
④ forget: 잊다 — 의미 다름
det.tip: 근거 없이 그럴 것이라 assume(추정) = suppose(가정하다)

det.korean: seriously=심각하게 / severely=심하게 / slightly=약간 / rarely=좀처럼 ~않는 / calmly=차분하게

③ rarely: 좀처럼 ~않는 — 의미 다름
④ calmly: 차분하게 — 의미 다름
det.tip: 기분에 seriously(심각하게) 영향을 줌 = severely(심하게)

questions.passage:
(A) Every weekend, she escapes the busy city to spend time in <u>nature</u>. Walking among the trees and rivers helps her relax and clear her mind.

(B) Although he snapped at me rudely, that behavior does not match his true <u>nature</u>. Deep down, he is a warm and patient person.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 nature의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: nature: (A) 자연 (B) 본성, 천성
det.analysis:
① (A) 자연 (B) 본성, 천성: spend time in nature=자연 속에서 시간을 보내다, his true nature=그의 진짜 본성 ←정답
② (A) 본성 (B) 자연: (A) 도시를 벗어나 나무·강 사이를 걷는 곳은 '자연'
③ (A) 자연 (B) 종류: (B) 무례한 행동이 그의 진짜 '종류'와 안 맞다? '본성'이 맞음
④ (A) 종류 (B) 본성: (A) 부적절
det.tip: nature의 다의어: 자연(natural world) vs 본성·천성(character)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the conditions and facts that surround and affect a particular situation"

det.korean: decisions=결정 / personalities=성격 / instructions=지시 / circumstances=상황(어떤 상황을 둘러싸고 영향을 주는 조건과 사실들)
det.analysis:
① decisions: 결정 — 스스로 내리는 판단일 뿐
② personalities: 성격 — 사람의 기질을 뜻함
③ instructions: 지시 — 무엇을 하라는 안내
④ circumstances: 상황 — 특정 상황을 둘러싸고 영향을 주는 조건과 사실들 ←정답
det.tip: conditions + facts + surround a situation = 상황(circumstances)

questions.passage: His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have __________ (contribute) to his or her actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: contribute(동사: 원인이 되다) → contributed. 'may have + 과거분사'는 '~했을지도 모른다'라는 과거의 추측
det.analysis: 동사 contribute을 과거분사 contributed로 바꿔요. 'may have contributed'는 '조동사 may + have + 과거분사' 구조로 '~의 원인이 되었을지도 모른다'라는 과거에 대한 추측을 나타내요. 그래서 원형 contribute이 아니라 과거분사 contributed가 필요해요.
det.tip: may have + 과거분사 = ~했을지도 모른다. contribute → contributed

questions.passage: When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while __________ (ignore) possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: ignore(동사: 무시하다) → ignoring. 접속사 while 뒤에서 '~하면서'를 나타내는 분사구문의 현재분사
det.analysis: 동사 ignore을 현재분사 ignoring으로 바꿔요. 'while ignoring ~'은 'while + 동사원형'이 아니라, '~하면서'라는 동시 동작을 나타내는 분사구문이라 -ing 형태가 필요해요. 여기서는 '가능한 원인을 무시하면서'라는 능동 의미라 현재분사 ignoring이 맞아요.
det.tip: while + -ing = ~하면서(동시 동작). ignore → ignoring

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably assume that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have __________ these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have good reasons for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: led to=~을 초래하다 / resulted from=~에서 비롯되다 / dealt with=~을 다루다 / looked for=~을 찾다
det.analysis:
① led to: ~을 초래하다 — 원인과 결과 방향이 반대
② resulted from: 그의 대답은 (본성이 아니라) 이런 상황'에서 비롯되었을' 수 있음 ←정답
③ dealt with: ~을 다루다 — 문맥 부적절
④ looked for: ~을 찾다 — 문맥 부적절
det.tip: His response may have __________ these circumstances (상황이 원인) → resulted from(~에서 비롯되다)

questions.passage: Imagine that you ask a man for directions, and he gives you a rude response. You will probably assume that he has an unpleasant personality. In fact, though, he might have just received some terrible news that has seriously affected his mood. His response may have resulted from these circumstances, not from his true nature. It is quite common to blame someone's personality without considering situational factors that may have contributed to his or her actions. What is especially interesting is that, while we often do this to other people, we rarely do it to ourselves. When looking at our own actions, we always believe that we have __________ for the things we do. However, we are quick to judge others negatively while ignoring possible contributing factors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: good reasons=타당한 이유 / bad intentions=나쁜 의도 / no choice=선택의 여지 없음 / little time=시간 부족
det.analysis:
① good reasons: 자신의 행동에는 늘 '타당한 이유'가 있다고 믿음 ←정답
② bad intentions: 나쁜 의도? 자신을 변호하는 흐름과 반대
③ no choice: 선택의 여지 없음? we have와 안 맞음
④ little time: 시간 부족? 문맥 무관
det.tip: 자신의 행동은 정당화함 → we always believe that we have __________ → 타당한 이유(good reasons)
